# Pandora Papers: King Abdullah II’s Reported Offshore Property Network

## Executive summary

The available reporting describes King Abdullah II of Jordan as the reported beneficial owner or ultimate beneficiary of a substantial portfolio of luxury properties in the United States and the United Kingdom. The reported structure involved offshore accounts, front companies, and offshore companies—especially entities incorporated in the British Virgin Islands (BVI)—that allegedly obscured ownership of the properties. The reported portfolio included properties in Malibu, Washington, DC, Ascot, and central London. [SRC-001] [SRC-002] [SRC-003]

The strongest reported figures are:

- **14 houses and flats** in the United States and United Kingdom;
- acquisitions between **2003 and 2017**;
- a reported total of more than **€91 million, or approximately $106 million**;
- use of **36 front companies registered in tax havens**; and
- three Malibu mansions reportedly acquired through **three offshore companies** for **$68 million**. [SRC-001] [SRC-003]

The evidence does not provide the names of the companies, trusts, accounts, directors, shareholders, nominees, accountants, or individual advisers involved. It specifically links Abdullah’s reported offshore companies to the **BVI**, but it does not establish that his entities were located in every jurisdiction mentioned in general descriptions of the Pandora Papers, such as Panama, Belize, Cyprus, the United Arab Emirates, Singapore, Switzerland, the Cook Islands, or South Dakota. [SRC-002] [SRC-003]

The reporting presents the offshore arrangements as a matter of public interest and political accountability. It does **not**, on the supplied evidence, establish that Abdullah committed money laundering, tax evasion, corruption, or misuse of public or foreign-aid funds. His lawyers, DLA Piper, and the Royal Hashemite Court denied misuse of public money and said the properties were purchased with personal wealth for privacy, security, diplomatic visits, and private use. [SRC-001] [SRC-002] [SRC-003]

## Scope and evidentiary categories

The evidence consists of reporting by DW, The Guardian, Al Jazeera, and an excerpt labeled as an ICIJ article. The materials contain several different kinds of information:

- **Reported facts:** statements attributed to leaked Pandora Papers records or to the royal palace and lawyers.
- **Allegations or reported findings:** claims that Abdullah used offshore structures to acquire properties and disguise ownership.
- **Assessments:** comments by journalists, experts, political figures, or analysts.
- **Context:** information about Jordanian aid, austerity, political dissatisfaction, and public reaction.
- **Unresolved uncertainty:** missing company names, incomplete ownership chains, unclear valuation bases, and an inability to reconcile all reported properties with all reported entities.

The existence of an offshore company or the use of a tax haven is not, by itself, evidence of criminal conduct. The supplied reporting states that offshore ownership can have legitimate privacy or security purposes and is not inherently illegal. [SRC-001] [SRC-002] [SRC-003]

## Core network reconstruction

### King Abdullah II

King Abdullah II is identified as a prominent person named in the Pandora Papers investigation. The reporting attributes to leaked records a network of offshore companies, offshore accounts, and front companies connected to his property acquisitions. [SRC-001] [SRC-002] [SRC-003]

DW reports that trust-firm sources referred to Abdullah as the “final beneficiary” living in Jordan, or used the phrase “You know who” from Jordan. This is a description reported from unnamed trust-firm sources; the supplied excerpt does not identify the relevant trust, company, account, or legal documentation. [SRC-001]

The Guardian reports that Abdullah’s ownership was disguised through a series of offshore companies incorporated in the BVI. Al Jazeera describes the broader arrangement as a network of offshore companies and tax havens used to build a property empire worth about $100 million. [SRC-002] [SRC-003]

### Offshore accounts

DW reports that Abdullah used money from various offshore accounts to purchase properties between 2003 and 2017. The accounts themselves are not named, and the evidence does not identify the banks, account numbers, account holders, or transfers associated with them. [SRC-001]

Accordingly, the supported relationship is:

> **King Abdullah II → reportedly used money from unnamed offshore accounts → to acquire properties**

The funding trail cannot be reconstructed further from the supplied evidence.

### Front companies

DW reports that Abdullah acquired 14 houses and flats in the United States and United Kingdom through 36 front companies registered in tax havens. [SRC-001]

The evidence does not establish:

- the names of the 36 companies;
- whether each company owned one property or multiple properties;
- whether the companies were subsidiaries of one another;
- whether all 36 were directly connected to property ownership;
- whether all 36 were incorporated in the BVI; or
- whether the three Malibu companies were included within the total of 36.

The supported relationship is therefore:

> **36 unnamed front companies → reportedly used in the acquisition of 14 US and UK properties → connected in reporting to King Abdullah II**

### Offshore companies used for Malibu properties

Al Jazeera reports that three beachfront mansions in Malibu were purchased through three offshore companies for $68 million by the King of Jordan. The companies are not named. [SRC-003]

The Guardian separately reports that Abdullah acquired three clifftop properties on the Malibu coast and describes the most expensive purchase as a 26-room, resort-like mansion overlooking the Malibu coastline. [SRC-002]

The supported relationship is:

> **Three unnamed offshore companies → reportedly used to purchase three Malibu mansions → reported purchaser or beneficial owner: King Abdullah II**

It remains unresolved whether these three companies form part of the 36 front companies reported by DW.

### Legal advisers and representatives

#### DLA Piper

DLA Piper is identified as the law firm representing the monarch. It denied that ownership through offshore jurisdictions was improper and stated that Abdullah had not misused public money or proceeds of aid intended for public use. [SRC-003]

No individual DLA Piper lawyer is named. The available evidence therefore supports a relationship between **DLA Piper and the royal representation**, but not between any named individual lawyer and a particular company, property, transaction, or account.

#### Unnamed lawyers

DW reports that the king’s lawyers rejected claims that Abdullah used money that was not his own. Al Jazeera reports that the lawyers said the properties were acquired with personal wealth and that high-profile individuals commonly use offshore companies for privacy and security. [SRC-001] [SRC-003]

The individual lawyers are not identified.

#### Trust-firm sources

Unnamed trust-firm sources reportedly referred to Abdullah as the “final beneficiary.” No trust firm, employee, trustee, adviser, or corporate-services provider is named. [SRC-001]

### Royal Hashemite Court and palace

The Royal Hashemite Court or royal palace confirmed that Abdullah owns properties abroad. Its explanation was that the properties were used for diplomatic visits, consultations, and some private visits, and that secrecy was important for security and privacy. [SRC-001] [SRC-003]

The palace and lawyers stated that:

- the properties were personally funded;
- the purchases were not funded by the state budget or treasury;
- no foreign grants or loans received as foreign assistance were used; and
- Abdullah had not misused public money or assistance intended for public use. [SRC-001] [SRC-003]

These statements are denials and explanations by representatives. They do not independently establish the source of Abdullah’s personal wealth or provide a property-by-property funding trail.

## Jurisdictions

### British Virgin Islands

The BVI is the only jurisdiction specifically linked in the supplied excerpts to Abdullah’s offshore companies. The Guardian reports that the companies used to disguise ownership were incorporated there. [SRC-002]

This supports the following relationship:

> **Unnamed offshore companies associated with Abdullah → reportedly incorporated in the British Virgin Islands**

The evidence does not provide the names of those entities or establish how many of the reported 36 front companies were BVI companies.

### Tax havens

DW characterizes the 36 front companies as registered in tax havens. Al Jazeera describes a network of offshore companies and tax havens. [SRC-001] [SRC-003]

“Tax havens” is used as a category rather than as a precise list of jurisdictions connected to each Abdullah-related entity.

### Other jurisdictions mentioned in the general Pandora Papers discussion

The supplied reporting mentions Panama, Belize, Cyprus, the United Arab Emirates, Singapore, Switzerland, the Cook Islands, and South Dakota in general explanations of the Pandora Papers and offshore service providers. [SRC-002] [SRC-003]

The evidence does not establish that Abdullah owned, controlled, or used an entity in any of those jurisdictions. They should therefore not be included in the reconstructed Abdullah network as confirmed locations.

## Reported property portfolio

### Malibu, California

The reporting identifies three Malibu properties:

- described by The Guardian as clifftop properties on the Malibu coast;
- described by Al Jazeera as beachfront mansions;
- reportedly purchased through three unnamed offshore companies;
- collectively reported by Al Jazeera to have cost $68 million. [SRC-002] [SRC-003]

One property is described as a 26-room, resort hotel-like mansion overlooking the Malibu coastline. The supplied evidence does not give its address, acquisition date, holding company, or separate purchase price. [SRC-002]

### Washington, DC

Al Jazeera reports that Abdullah owns three luxury apartments in a Washington, DC, complex with panoramic views of the Potomac River. [SRC-003]

The complex, address, acquisition dates, prices, and holding companies are not identified.

### Ascot, England

Al Jazeera reports that Abdullah owns a house in Ascot, described as one of England’s expensive towns. [SRC-003]

The address, price, acquisition date, and legal owner are not provided.

### Central London

The reporting identifies multimillion-dollar apartments in central London. The Guardian refers to exclusive central London postcodes, while Al Jazeera describes multimillion-dollar apartments. [SRC-002] [SRC-003]

The number of apartments, addresses, prices, acquisition dates, and holding companies are not specified.

### Portfolio-wide figures

DW reports 14 houses and flats in the United States and United Kingdom, acquired from 2003 to 2017 for more than €91 million, or approximately $106 million, through 36 front companies. [SRC-001]

The Guardian describes the portfolio as worth well in excess of $100 million. Al Jazeera calls it a $100 million property empire. [SRC-002] [SRC-003]

These figures are not fully reconciled. They may refer to different valuation methods, purchase-price totals, rounded estimates, or different subsets of the portfolio. The supplied material does not say whether the figures represent acquisition costs, current market values, or another measure.

## Chronology

- **2003–2017:** DW reports that Abdullah used offshore accounts to acquire properties during this period. [SRC-001]
- **After the Arab Spring protests:** Al Jazeera places the Malibu purchases in the years after protests in Jordan, but gives no exact transaction dates. [SRC-003]
- **October 3, 2021:** The Guardian and Al Jazeera published reporting on the Pandora Papers revelations. [SRC-002] [SRC-003]
- **October 4, 2021:** DW published its report, and Al Jazeera updated its article. [SRC-001] [SRC-003]

The Pandora Papers dataset is described as containing records dating back to the 1970s, with most files covering 1996–2020. That describes the overall dataset, not necessarily the dates of Abdullah’s individual transactions. [SRC-002] [SRC-003]

## Financial-aid and political context

The reporting places the property disclosures in the context of Jordan’s dependence on international financial assistance, austerity, and public concern over economic conditions. The Guardian reports that US economic and military aid to Jordan increased while citizens faced austerity connected to an International Monetary Fund bailout. [SRC-002]

DW reports that Jordan received substantial development aid from the United States, the European Union, Germany, and other countries, including approximately $1.5 billion in US aid in 2020. [SRC-001]

The available evidence does not establish that aid money financed Abdullah’s properties. DW reports that, according to current knowledge, development aid had not been funneled to the palace. A German development ministry spokesperson likewise said the ministry had no knowledge that its development-cooperation funds had been made available to the royal family. [SRC-001]

The connection between aid and the property story is therefore contextual and political, not a demonstrated funding link.

## Public reaction and expert assessments

The Guardian reports that Jordanian lawyer Moayyad al-Majali was detained in 2019 after asking how much land the king owned. This is reported political context, not evidence that al-Majali had a role in the offshore property structure. [SRC-002]

DW reports public discontent following the Pandora Papers revelations. Karim Merhej described the disclosures as validating concerns held by many Jordanians, while Maria Josua said it had long been known that the royal family was wealthy and owned property abroad. These are assessments, not evidence of the legal ownership structure. [SRC-001]

Annelle Sheline commented on the political sensitivity of a Jordanian monarch displaying wealth while Western donors provided assistance. Sven Giegold characterized the leak as a reason to strengthen measures against global tax evasion and inequality. Neither statement establishes tax evasion or wrongdoing by Abdullah. [SRC-003]

DW also discusses Queen Rania, Prince Hamzah, and Bassem Awadallah in the broader political context of Jordan. The supplied evidence does not connect any of them to Abdullah’s offshore companies, property purchases, accounts, or advisers. [SRC-001]

## What the evidence establishes—and what it does not

### Supported conclusions

The supplied evidence supports the following conclusions:

1. Public reporting based on the Pandora Papers connected King Abdullah II to a large offshore-held property portfolio.
2. The reported portfolio included properties in Malibu, Washington, DC, Ascot, and central London.
3. Reporting described 14 US and UK houses and flats acquired between 2003 and 2017.
4. DW reported the use of 36 front companies registered in tax havens.
5. Al Jazeera reported that three unnamed offshore companies were used to acquire three Malibu mansions for $68 million.
6. The Guardian specifically linked Abdullah’s reported offshore companies to the BVI.
7. DLA Piper and unnamed royal lawyers denied misuse of public funds and said the properties were funded with personal wealth.
8. The royal palace confirmed ownership of foreign properties and cited privacy, security, diplomatic visits, and private use as explanations.
9. No supplied source establishes criminal conduct by Abdullah.

### Unsupported or unresolved conclusions

The evidence does not establish:

- the names of any Abdullah-related shell or front companies;
- the identity of any trust, foundation, bank, account, trustee, director, shareholder, nominee, accountant, or individual adviser;
- the complete ownership chain for any property;
- whether the three Malibu companies were among the 36 front companies;
- the exact number of London properties;
- the addresses or individual prices of the properties;
- the source of Abdullah’s personal wealth;
- whether any state resources or foreign aid were indirectly connected to the personal funds;
- that Abdullah used entities in jurisdictions other than the BVI;
- that Abdullah committed tax evasion, money laundering, corruption, or another offense.

## Contradictions and evidence gaps

### Number and valuation of properties

The reported figures differ:

- more than €91 million, or $106 million, for 14 houses and flats;
- a portfolio worth well in excess of $100 million; and
- a $100 million property empire. [SRC-001] [SRC-002] [SRC-003]

The sources do not state whether these are purchase prices, current values, rounded estimates, or different subsets of the portfolio.

### Relationship between 36 companies and three Malibu companies

The reporting identifies 36 front companies for the broader US and UK portfolio and three offshore companies for the Malibu purchases. It does not say whether the three Malibu companies are included in the 36-company count. [SRC-001] [SRC-003]

### Incomplete property reconciliation

The named locations account for three Malibu properties, three Washington apartments, one Ascot house, and an unspecified number of central London apartments. The excerpts do not reconcile these descriptions to all 14 reported houses and flats. [SRC-001] [SRC-003]

### Source-label discrepancy

SRC-004 is labeled with an ICIJ URL, but the supplied excerpt duplicates the Al Jazeera article, including its wording and presentation. It should not be treated as an independent account adding separate facts beyond those supported by SRC-003. [SRC-003] [SRC-004]

### No named legal vehicles or intermediaries

Although the reporting refers to front companies, offshore companies, offshore accounts, and a final beneficiary, it does not identify any specific legal vehicle or individual intermediary. DLA Piper is the only named professional organization connected to the royal response, and the evidence does not identify a particular DLA Piper lawyer or transaction. [SRC-001] [SRC-002] [SRC-003]

## Sources

- [SRC-001] **Pandora Papers: The royal ‘you know who’ from Jordan** — https://www.dw.com/en/pandora-papers-the-king-of-jordans-hidden-property-gems/a-59403014
- [SRC-002] **King of Jordan hidden property empire worth more than $100m, Pandora papers reveal** — https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal
- [SRC-003] **Investigation reveals offshore assets of heads of state** — https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/3/investigation-reveals-offshore-assets-of-heads-of-state
- [SRC-004] **While foreign aid poured in, Jordan’s King Abdullah funnelled $100 million into luxury homes** — https://www.icij.org/investigations/pandora-papers/jordan-king-abdullah-luxury-property/
